en: Outer Title: Catalogue of the Dharma Sought by the Japanese Bhikṣu Enchin upon Entering Tang China,
at Guoqing Temple on Mount Tiantai.

Catalogue of the Dharma Sought by Enchin, a monk of Enryaku-ji on Mount Hiei in the Capital of the Kingdom of Japan, upon his arrival in Chang’an: Having arrived at the city of Chang’an, he obtained the religious teachings of the Vairocana school.
The images, ritual implements,
and the scriptural texts taught by the Great Master Zhiyi preserved at Guoqing Chan Monastery and other temples.
These epigraphic inscriptions and other documents,
together with the various petitions and memorials obtained from the provinces,
total three hundred and forty-one items.
Seven hundred and seventy-two fascicles,
as well as Sanskrit manuscripts, ritual implements, and so forth;
in total, there were seventeen items counted from beginning to end.
I respectfully set forth the titles as follows:
The Vairocana Religious Teachings, along with Iconography and Ritual Implements. The total number of religious teachings, iconographies, and items amounts to one hundred and seventeen volumes.
One hundred and fifty-eight fascicles.
There are ten ritual implements.

*The Mahāvairocana Sūtra on the Attainment of Buddhahood*, one volume in seven fascicles; *The Sūtra of the Concise Recitation Extracted from the Yoga of Vajraśekhara*, one volume in four or six fascicles. The above two works are recorded in the *Kaiyuan Catalogue of Buddhist Teachings*.
*The Dharma Prohibition of One Hundred Transformations of Vajra Kṣitigarbha*, one fascicle; *The Exposition of the Supernatural Methods by Vajra Kṣitigarbha*, one fascicle;
*The Original Text of the Great Compassion Heart Dhāraṇī of the Thousand-Handed and Thousand-Eyed Avalokiteśvara*, one fascicle;
*The Vajraśekhara Sūtra: The Method of Vairocana Samādhi*, one fascicle; and *The Secret Dhāraṇī of the Messenger of Acala*.
*The Dharma in One Volume*; *The Yoga of the Vajraśekhara Sūtra: The Chapter on the Dharma of Mañjuśrī Bodhisattva in One Volume*;
*The Mahāsukha-vajra-amoghasiddhi-satya-samaya Sūtra in One Volume*; *The Vajraśekhara-yoga Akṣasūtra in One Volume*;
*The Sarvatathāgata-vajrāyus-dhāraṇī Sūtra in One Volume*; *The Ekākṣara*.
*The Sūtra of the Extraordinary Buddha-Uṣṇīṣa*, three fascicles; *The Vast Ritual Manual of the Vajra-Terifying Assembly*, one fascicle;
*The Sūtra of Ālidala Aruli*, one fascicle; *The Liturgy of Mañjuśrī’s Praise of the Dharmakāya*, one fascicle;
*The Mahāyāna Sūtra of the Twelve Mudrās and One Hundred and Eight Names of the Auspicious Goddess*, one fascicle; *The Complete [Teachings] of All Tathāgatas*.
*Śarīra-ratna-kaṭāha-mudrā-dhāraṇī-sūtra*, one fascicle; *Tattvasamaya-sūtra*, one fascicle;
*Ekādaśamukha-avalokiteśvara-bodhisattva-vidhi-sūtra*, three fascicles; *Śrī-devī-dvādaśanāma-sūtra*, one fascicle;
*Vajraśekhara-yoga-aṣṭādaśa-parivarta-tātparya-nirdeśa*, one fascicle; *Vajraśekhara-vibhāga*.
*The Dharma Gate of the Distinctive Noble Stages*, one fascicle; *The Mañjuśrī-mūla-tantra (Cakravartin King Spoken at the Site of Enlightenment)*, five fascicles;
*The Vajra-Āyus-dhāraṇī Sūtra*, one fascicle; *The Mahāmāyūrī-vidyārājñī Sūtra*, three fascicles;
*The Ritual for Making Offerings to Tathāgata Amitāyus*, one fascicle; *The Mahāmegha-cakra Rain-invoking Sūtra*, two fascicles; and *The Bestowal upon the Hungry Ghosts of the Flaming Mouth*.
*Dhāraṇī Sūtra*, one fascicle; *Bodhimaṇḍala-vyūha-dhāraṇī Sūtra*, one fascicle;
*Sumāhuka-kumāra Sūtra*, two fascicles or three fascicles; *Aṣṭamahābodhisattva-maṇḍala Sūtra*, one fascicle;
*Pāṇḍaravāsinī-avalokiteśvara-bodhisattva Sūtra*, one fascicle; *Vaiśravaṇa-rāja-devaputra Sūtra*, one fascicle; *Vajraśekhara-padma...* [text fragment].
*The Flower Family Heart Mantra Recitation Method*, two fascicles (or one fascicle, or four fascicles); *The Vajraśekhara Yoga Thousand-Handed and Thousand-Eyed Recitation Method*, one fascicle;
*The Recitation Method of Akṣobhya Tathāgata*, one fascicle; *The Recitation Ritual of the One-Syllable Uṣṇīṣa Cakra King*, one fascicle;
*The Yoga Sūtra of the One-Syllable Uṣṇīṣa Cakra King*, one fascicle; *The Buddha-Uṣṇīṣa*.
One fascicle: *The Ritual Manual for the Recitation of the Uṣṇīṣavijaya Dhāraṇī*. One fascicle: *The Method for Recitation of the Vajraśekhara Supreme Yoga*.
One fascicle: *The Method for Recitation of Vajrāyus*. One fascicle: *The Secret Sūtra for Recitation of Vajrarāja Bodhisattva*. One fascicle:
*The Ritual Manual for Recitation of Samantabhadra-Vajrasattva*. *Vajraśekhara Yoga*... [text fragment]
One fascicle of the *Gaṇacakra-vidhi* (or alternatively, the *Mahāsukha-vajrasattva-vidhi*, or the *Mahāsukha-vajrasattva-pañca-rahasya-vidhi*);
one fascicle of the *Rājanīti-prajñā-pāramitā-japa-vidhi*; one fascicle of the *Cintāmaṇicakra-japa-vidhi*;
one fascicle of the *Mahākāśyapa-garbha-japa-vidhi*; and [the rites for] the Holy Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva.
One scroll: *The Ritual Manual for the Heart Mantra*. One scroll: *The Method of Recitation for the Yoga Lotus Family*. One scroll:
*The Method of Recitation for the Bodhisattva Tārā from the Vajraśekhara Sūtra*. One scroll: *The Yoga Method of Recitation for Amṛtakuṇḍalī*.
One scroll: *The Ritual for Receiving the Bodhicitta Precepts*. One scroll: *The Vajraśekhara Yoga Prostration to the Thirty-seven Honored Ones*.
One fascicle: *Catalogue of Dhāraṇīs of the General Section* (*Doubu dharani mu*). One fascicle: *Exposition on the Meaning of the Seventeen Honored Ones of the Great Maṇḍala*.
One fascicle: *Ritual Manual for Vajraśekhara Yoga Homa*. One fascicle: *Saptakoṭi-Buddhamātṛ-dhāraṇī-sūtra*. One fascicle:
*Ritual Manual for the Accomplishment of the King of the Lotus Sūtra*. *Vajraśekhara-vijaya-ādi* [fragment].
*Recitation Ritual* (Niansong yigui), one fascicle; *Sādhana of the Great Yakṣa’s Beloved Son* (Dayeqia aizizi chengjufa), one fascicle;

*Commentary on the Meaning of the Mahāsukha-vajra-amoghasiddhi-samaya-sūtra* (Dale jin'gang bukong zhenshi sanmeiyi jing yishu), one fascicle; *Universal Radiance Mahāpratisarā Dhāraṇī Sūtra* (Pubian guangming da suiqiu tuoluoni jing), two fascicles;
*Verses on the Five-Syllable Dhāraṇī* (Wuzi tuoluoni song), one fascicle; *The Fierce Wrath of the Holy Yamāntaka* (Sheng yanman deka weinu).
*The Royal Law*, one fascicle; *The Recitation Method for the Holy Yamāntaka, King of Wrath*, one fascicle;
*The Ritual Manual for the Accomplishment of the Greatly Majestic and Wrathful Ucchuṣma*, one fascicle;

*The Scripture on the Ritual Manual for the Accomplishment of the Bodhisattva Ārya-Kani-Krodha-Vajrakumāra*, three fascicles; *The Dhāraṇī Scripture of the One-Knot Honored One*, one fascicle; *Vajraśekhara*.
One fascicle of the *Sūtra on the Ritual Manual for the Recitation of the One-Syllable Cakravartin King*, with swift and immediate efficacy;
one fascicle of the *Exposition of the Method for the Kinnara-Aveśa*; one fascicle of the *Method for Following the Seven-Limb Recitation of Mahāvairocana*;
one fascicle of the *Brief Compendium of the Method for Following the Recitation of the Mahāvairocana Sūtra*; and the *Great Ritual of Vajraśekhara Trailokyavijaya*.
*Vajraśekhara-sūtra-yoga-mañjuśrī-bodhisattva-vidhi-kalpa*, one fascicle;
*Vajraśekhara-sūtra-avalokiteśvara-rāja-tathāgata-caryā-dharma*, one fascicle;
*Mañjuśrī-nakṣatra-sūtra*, two fascicles; *Vajraśekhara-samyaksambodhicitta-śāstra*, one fascicle; *Prajñāpāramitā-bhāvanā*.
*The Ritual Manual for the Profound Contemplation Practice*, one fascicle; *The Commentary on the Benevolent Kings Prajñāpāramitā Dhāraṇī*, one fascicle;
*The Method of Recitation for the Accomplishment of the Great Compassion of Avalokiteśvara*, one fascicle; *The Sūtra of the Radiant Empowerment of Vajrapāṇi*, one fascicle;
*The Ritual Manual for the Iconography of Mahāmāyūrī Vidyārājñī*, one fascicle; and *The Essential Summary of Recitation for the Buddha-uṣṇīṣa of the Golden-Wheel King*.
*The Dharma of the Great Sage, the Joyful Double-Body Vināyaka*, one fascicle;
*The Yoga Recitation Method of Avalokiteśvara Bodhisattva’s Wish-Fulfilling Wheel*, one fascicle; *The Ritual for the Practice and Recitation of the Vajraśekhara Yoga Samantabhadra*, one fascicle;
and *The Catalogue of the Buddhist Teachings Compiled during the Zhenyuan Era*, one fascicle—all of the above are recorded in the *Zhenyuan shijiao mulu*.
*Yuan shijiao lu* (A Record of Buddhist Teachings from the Yuan Dynasty).
*Dapilushena jing yishu* (Commentary on the Meaning of the Mahāvairocana Sūtra), one work in ten fascicles; one manuscript of the *Mahāvairocana Sūtra Mantra* in Sanskrit script;
one manuscript of the *Vairocana Universal Offering Praise* in Sanskrit script; and [one manuscript of] the *Vajra* in Sanskrit script.
One volume of the *Uṣṇīṣavijaya-dhāraṇī* in Sanskrit script; one volume of the *Mahāmāyūrī-vidyārājñī-sūtra* mantras in Sanskrit script;

one volume of the *Mahāmaṅgala-gāthā* (The Great Auspicious Verses) in nine stanzas, transcribed in comparison with the canonical text in Sanskrit script; one scroll of the *Siddham* characters in Sanskrit script;
one scroll of the Sanskrit names of the various deities on the faces of the Womb Realm (*Garbhadhātu*) maṇḍala; [and] the Sanskrit name of the Bodhisattva Samantabhadra.
One fascicle of the *Gāthā on the Vows of Practice* (Caryāpraṇidhānagāthā); one scroll of the *Great Uṣṇīṣa Dhāraṇī* in Sanskrit characters;
one fascicle of the *Mahāpratihārya Dhāraṇī* in Sanskrit characters; one fascicle of the *Mahākāya Dhāraṇī of the Thousand-Armed Avalokiteśvara* in Sanskrit characters;
one fascicle of the *Sanskrit Mahākaruṇā Root Dhāraṇī*; and one fascicle of the *Sanskrit Vimalaviśuddhi*.
One manuscript of the *Kiraṇa-mantra* in Sanskrit script; one manuscript of the *Cūḍā-śikhara-mantra* in Sanskrit script;
one manuscript of the *Stūpa-nirmāṇa-mantra* in Sanskrit script—these to be placed within the central axis (*yaṣṭi*) of the *cūḍāmaṇi* and around the perimeter of the stūpa;

one manuscript of the *Mantrarāja-dharmaparyāya-mantra* in Sanskrit script to be placed inside the stūpa according to the ritual of the *Mantrarāja*; one manuscript of the *Cūḍāmaṇi-mantra* in Sanskrit script; and the *Dharmakāya-gāthā*.
One scroll of a Sanskrit text: Praise to the Lotus Family (*Padmakula*). One scroll of a Sanskrit text: The Uṣṇīṣavijayā Dhāraṇī.
One scroll of a Sanskrit text: The Trailokyavijaya Amoghapāśa Dhāraṇī.
One set of five scrolls of the *Mahāvairocana Tathāgata Mahākaruṇā-garbha-maṇḍala*. Nine sets of the *Vajradhātu Navasamāja Maṇḍala*.
One set of six mandala surfaces for the eighty-one deities of the Vajradhātu;
one set of four mandalas for the Mahāvairocana Navavyūha Cakravartin;
one set of six mandala surfaces for the Dharma-maṇḍala of the eighty-one deities of the Vajradhātu; one consecration samaya five-pronged vajra. Five.
One vajra-bell with a vajra-handle; two items above this were transmitted from the teachings of Master He; four *dharma-mudrā-karmavajras*;
four ritual stakes for consecrating the altar; and one scroll of the *Dharmaparyeṣaṇā-nidāna* (Catalogue of Sought Dharmas).
All of the above were obtained through transmission in the city of Chang’an.

The records of the Dharma Flower (Saddharmapuṇḍarīka) teachings and their commentaries, along with inscriptions on steles, transmitted by the Great Master Zhizhe of Tiantai, totaling sixty-seven works in two hundred twenty-seven fascicles.

The Tiantai commentaries and outlines for the *Saddharmapuṇḍarīka-sūtra* in one volume and seven fascicles; the *Miaofa lianhua jing xuan yi* (Profound Meaning of the Lotus Sutra) in ten volumes; the two versions of the *Fahua wenju* (Words and Phrases of the Lotus Sutra) in twenty volumes; the *Fahua shuji* (Commentary on the Commentary on the Lotus Sutra) in ten volumes; the *Fahua xuan yi lue yao* (Abridged Essentials of the Profound Meaning of the Lotus Sutra) in one volume; the *Fahua ke wen* (Outline of the Lotus Sutra) in two volumes; the *Fahua da yi* (General Meaning of the Lotus Sutra) in one volume; the *Fahua xuan yi ke wen* (Outline of the Profound Meaning of the Lotus Sutra) in two volumes; the *Fahua shu ke wen* (Outline of the Commentary on the Lotus Sutra) in one volume; the *Fahua xuan shi qian yuan qi xu* (Preface to the Origins of the Sub-commentary on the Profound Meaning of the Lotus Sutra) in one volume; the *Fahua wenju* in three volumes; the *Fahua wenju yi ke* (Categorized Outline of the Meaning of the Words and Phrases of the Lotus Sutra) in three volumes; the two versions of the *Fahua shuji* in twenty volumes; and the *Miaofa lianhua jing wenju zhupin yao yi* (Essential Meanings of the Various Chapters of the Words and Phrases of the Lotus Sutra) in one volume. The above constitute the section on the *Lotus Sutra*.

*Mahā-śamatha-vipaśyanā* (Mohe zhiguan), ten fascicles; *Mahā-śamatha-vipaśyanā*, fourteen fascicles; *Abridged Version of Mahā-śamatha-vipaśyanā*, six fascicles; *Sub-commentary on the Essentials of Śamatha-vipaśyanā Practice* (Zhiguan fuxing souyao ji), eleven fascicles; *Outline of Śamatha-vipaśyanā* (Zhiguan kewen), two fascicles; *Exemplars of the Meaning of Śamatha-vipaśyanā* (Zhiguan yili), one fascicle; *Revised Outline of Śamatha-vipaśyanā* (Zaikan ben zhiguan kewen), one fascicle; *General Exemplars of Śamatha-vipaśyanā* (Zhiguan tongli), one fascicle. The above constitute the section on *Śamatha-vipaśyanā*.

One copy of the *Suvarṇaprabhāsa-sūtra* in four fascicles; one fascicle of the *Suvarṇaprabhāsa-mysterious-meaning* (*Suvarṇaprabhāsa-xuan-yi*); three fascicles of the *Suvarṇaprabhāsa-word-interpretation* (*Suvarṇaprabhāsa-wen-ju*);

one fascicle of the *Suvarṇaprabhāsa-word-interpretation-outline* (*Suvarṇaprabhāsa-wen-ju-ke*); one fascicle of the *Essentials of the Chan Gate* (*Chan-men-yao-lüe*); one fascicle of the *Master Zhi’s Oral Instructions* (*Zhi-dashi-kou-jue*);

one fascicle of the *Method for Reciting Sutras by Contemplating the Mind along with the Text for Making Vows* (*Guanxin-songjing-fa bing fayuan-wen*); one fascicle of the *Treatise on Contemplating the Mind* (*Guanxin-lun*); [and] *Contemplation* (*Guan*).
*Commentary on the Heart Treatise Following the Text*, one fascicle; *A Single Copy for Contemplating the Mind and Reciting the Meaning of the Twelve Divisions of the Sūtras*, one fascicle;

*Brief Clarification for Opening the Darkness for Beginners: Essentials of Seated Meditation and Śamatha-Vipaśyanā*, one fascicle (also titled *Small Śamatha-Vipaśyanā* or divided into two fascicles);
*Ritual for Supplementing Deficiencies in the Vaipulya Repentance*, one fascicle; *Method for Contemplating Food*, one fascicle; *Commentary on the Diamond Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra*, one fascicle.
The Mahāparinirvāṇa Sūtra in thirty-eight fascicles; the Tiantai Commentary on the Mahāparinirvāṇa Sūtra in nine fascicles (the original manuscript was sought but not yet fully obtained);
the Profound Meaning of the Mahāparinirvāṇa Sūtra in one fascicle; the Revised Draft of the Commentary on the Mahāparinirvāṇa Sūtra in fifteen fascicles;
the Jingxi Re-edited Explanation in thirty-eight fascicles; and the *Jingangbei* in its entirety.

*Fajie Cidi Chumen* (The Ten Gates of the Gradual Progression of the Dharma Realm), one fascicle; *Bodhisattva-śīla-sūtra-yiji* (Record of the Meaning of the Bodhisattva Precepts Sūtra), two fascicles; *Daban Niepan Jing Kewen* (Outline of the Mahāparinirvāṇa Sūtra), five fascicles;
*Daban Niepan Jing Houfen Kewen* (Outline of the Latter Part of the Mahāparinirvāṇa Sūtra), one fascicle; *Daban Niepan Jing Zhu Kewen* (Annotated Outline of the Mahāparinirvāṇa Sūtra), one fascicle;
*Shangshidi Erbujimen Lun* (Treatise on the Ten Superiorities and the Two Non-dual Gates), one fascicle; and *Tiantai Dashi Jinguangming* (The Golden Light Sūtra by the Great Master Tiantai).
*Chanyi* (Ritual for Repentance), one fascicle; *Tiantai Dashi Liuzhi Liewen* (Text for the Six Periods of Worship by the Great Master Tiantai), one fascicle;

*Chenshuandi Shixiong Nanyue Sida Shi Beiwen* (Stele Inscription for the Great Master Sengzhi of Mount Nanyue, Preceptor of the Chen Dynasty), one fascicle; *Chensui Erguo Shixiong Tiantaishan Zhizhe Dashi Beiwen* (Stele Inscription for the Great Master Zhizhe of Mount Tiantai, Preceptor of the Chen and Sui Dynasties), one fascicle.
The two steles mentioned above are currently extant at the Qianfu Temple in the Right Street of Chang’an City, [housing] the Prabhūtaratna Stūpa.
This was composed by the Chan Master Chujin, a former disciple of the Dharma at the Stūpa Courtyard. One scroll:
"Epigraph for the Meditation Practice Center on Mount Tiantai. One scroll: "Epigraph for the Chan Forest Monastery on Buddha’s Ridge at Mount Tiantai.
[And] the lineage of the Sixth Patriarch of the Tiantai Master’s transmission of the Dharma, the late master of Jingxi Miaole Monastery, across various provinces.

One fascicle of the *Menren Hongjiao Lu* (Record of the Disciples’ Propagation of the Teaching); one fascicle of the *Tiantai Dashi Jingguangming Zhai Beiwen* (Stele Inscription for the Golden Light Assembly of the Great Master of Tiantai);

one fascicle of the *Tiantai Shan Xiaolu* (Small Record of Mount Tiantai); one copy of the *Yuezhou Meng Zhongcheng Xiuli Tiantai Shan Shixiang Daochang Beiwen* (Stele Inscription for the Stone Elephant Practice Hall on Mount Tiantai, repaired by Meng Zhongcheng of Yuezhou);

one fascicle of the *Tiantai Shi’er Suo Daochang Ji* (Record of the Twelve Monasteries and Practice Halls of Tiantai); and the *Shenshe Bo Ben Jingzang* (The Divinities Relinquish the Original Pine-Wood Scripture Repository).

One fascicle: Record of the Three Pavilions of Mount Tiantai; one fascicle: Epitaph for the Two Late Virtuous Bhikṣuṇīs of the Fahua Monastery at Tianxing Temple in Changzhou, Tang Dynasty (these three items combined into one scroll); one fascicle:
Biographical Account of the Late Vinaya Master of Guoqing Temple on Mount Tiantai; [one item: The Appointment of the Vinaya Master of Guoqing Temple on Mount Tiantai.
One fascicle of the *Yingzan* (Hymn to the Shadow), one fascicle of the stele inscription for the Great Master as cited by the Vinaya Virtuous One of Guoqing Temple,
and one scroll of the *Tiantai Xitan Zhang* (Tiantai’s Exposition on the Universal Discourse); these, together with the combined scroll of the Hymn to the Upādhyāya of Sizhou,
were all obtained at the two monasteries of Guoqing and Chanlin, as well as in the prefectures of Tiantai and Yue, among the commentaries and treatises of various schools.
In total, there are one hundred and fifty-seven works comprising three hundred and eighty-seven fascicles:

*The Profound Discussion on the Lotus Sūtra* (1 fascicle), *Preface to the Propagation of the Saddharmapuṇḍarīka Sūtra* (1 fascicle), *Mysterious Commentary on the Saddharmapuṇḍarīka Sūtra* in two versions (20 fascicles), *Excerpts from the Lotus Sūtra* (6 fascicles), and *Outline of the Lotus Sūtra* (2 fascicles). The *Dharma*... [text truncated]
*Huá míng xiàng* (Names and Characteristics of the Flowers), one fascicle; *Dà fāng guǎng fó huá yán jīng lùn* (Treatise on the Avataṃsaka Sūtra of the Buddha’s Great Vaipulya), forty fascicles;

*Huá yán jīng yì hǎi* (The Ocean of Meaning of the Avataṃsaka Sūtra), two fascicles; *Jīn shī zǐ guān mén* (The Gate of Contemplating the Golden Lion), one fascicle—these two works are combined into a single volume;

*Huá yán jīng shū* (Commentary on the Avataṃsaka Sūtra), twenty fascicles; *Huá yán jīng huán yuán guān* (Contemplation on Returning to the Source of the Avataṃsaka Sūtra), one fascicle; *Huá yán jīng sī jì* (Private Record of the Avataṃsaka Sūtra), two fascicles; *Huá yán jīng* (Avataṃsaka Sūtra).
*Fajie guan* (Contemplation of the Dharma Realm), one fascicle; *Duhuishun Heshang yuanqi* (The Origin Story of Venerable Duhuishun), one fascicle; the above two fascicles combined in one volume;

*Huayan shou putixin jie* (The Huayan Ritual for Receiving the Bodhicitta Precepts), one fascicle; *Pusa jie shu* (Commentary on the Bodhisattva Precepts), two fascicles; *Dacheng busa fa* (The Mahāyāna Method for the Poṣadha), one fascicle;

*Pusa xindi jieben* (The Bodhisattva Mind-Ground Precept Text), one fascicle; the above two fascicles combined in one volume; *Jingming jing Guanzhong shu* (The Commentary on the Vimalakīrti Sūtra from Guanzhong).
*Commentary on the Three-Scroll Vimalakīrti Sūtra* (Guāngzhōng Shùshì) in two scrolls; *Subtle Commentary on the Guāngzhōng Shùshì of the Vimalakīrti Sūtra* in two scrolls;
*Diagram of the Essential Meanings of the Guāngzhōng Shùshì of the Vimalakīrti Sūtra* in one scroll; *Record of the Vimalakīrti Sūtra* in two scrolls;
*Essential Summary Commentary on the Vimalakīrtinirdeśa Sūtra* in one scroll; *Exposition of the Correct Meaning of the Vimalakīrti Sūtra* in five scrolls.

*Jiqing yanzheng shuchao* (Exegesis on the *Zhengjue jing*), three fascicles; *Lengqie aboduoluo baojing* (The Precious Scripture of the Laṅkāvatāra), four fascicles; *Kedian lengqie baojing shu* (Annotated Outline of the Commentary on the Precious Laṅkāvatāra Scripture), ten fascicles;
*Amituo jing shu* (Commentary on the Amitābha Sūtra), one fascicle; *Jingang banruo jing shu* (Commentary on the Diamond Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra), three fascicles;

*Jingang banruo jing jue* (Manual on the Diamond Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra), one fascicle; *Jingang banruo jing yi* (Meaning of the Diamond Prajñāpāramitā Sūtra), one fascicle; *Zhuban* (Notes on the *Prajñāpāramitā*).
*Heart Sūtra*, one fascicle; *Commentary on the Heart Sūtra of Prajñā*, one fascicle; *New Translation of the Opening of the Benevolent Kings Sūtra*, one fascicle;
*Commentary on the Benevolent Kings Prajñā Sūtra*, two fascicles; *Outline of the Benevolent Kings Sūtra*, one fascicle;

*Search for the Profound Record of the Commentary on the Benevolent Kings Prajñā*, two fascicles; *Essential Record of the Commentary on the Benevolent Kings Prajñā*, one fascicle; *Commentary on the Benevolent Kings Prajñā*.

*Yaoji* (Essential Record) in two fascicles; *Daban Niepan Jing Yiji* (Record of the Meaning of the Mahāparinirvāṇa-sūtra) in ten fascicles; *Shimumen Lun Shu* (Commentary on the Dvādaśamukha-śāstra) in one fascicle;
*Shimumen Lun Shu Xuanyi* (Profound Meaning of the Commentary on the Dvādaśamukha-śāstra) in one fascicle; *Shimumen Lun Shu Ji* (Record of the Commentary on the Dvādaśamukha-śāstra) in one fascicle;

*Shang Dacheng Baifa Mingmen Lun Yichao* (Excerpts on the Meaning of the Mahāyāna-śatadharma-viśāradā-mukha-śāstra) in two fascicles; and *Cheng Weishi Lun Bashen Sanyong Tu* (Diagram of the Eight Consciousnesses and Three Bodies according to the Vijñaptimātratāsiddhi-śāstra) in one fascicle.

In the provinces of Wenzhou, Taizhou, Yuezhou, and others, I sought out and obtained various fragments of sutras and śāstras, though their volumes were incomplete; furthermore,

The Dharma objects brought by the Brahmin, including the aforementioned items brought by the Brahmin, were all lacquered.

Among them were: one Sanskrit manuscript in a bamboo slip case from the Mahānālandā Monastery in Central India; one Sanskrit manuscript on *pātra* leaves from before the Buddha Hall of the Mahānālandā Monastery in Central India; and one five-pronged vajra scepter made of refined copper with a finger-ring attached—these three items were on the right.
These are all the Tripiṭaka of the Brahmins,
brought from India by Enchin in the autumn of the seventh year of the Dàzhōng era.
Upon arriving in Fuzhou, he met the Tripiṭaka Master,
from whom he studied the *Siddham* script of the Brahmā Heaven and was instructed in various Sanskrit scriptures and other texts.
It is traditionally said that these items were to remain in this country forever for the purpose of making offerings:
one staff of *pippala* wood from India, one staff of rattan from Guangzhou, one catty of white mustard seeds, and one glass bottle— these four articles.
All of these were sent from Guangzhou by the monk Qu Sengtian Yuanjue on your behalf.

They consist of one scroll of the catalog of scriptures and teachings sought by the Japanese monk Enchin of Enryaku-ji on Mount Hiei in the capital of Japan during his study tour in Tang China, including the two divisions of the Esoteric Teachings (Shingon) of our former school.
As well as the commentaries and sub-commentaries of other schools,
inscriptions, steles, Sanskrit manuscripts,
ritual objects, and their respective catalogs.
I have obtained these items to the best of my ability.
A full inventory is recorded here as previously detailed.
Respectfully inscribed.
Recorded on the [blank] day of the tenth month in the eleventh year of the Dazhong era of the Great Tang by the Japanese monk Enchin, a seeker of the Dharma.
